headline: Meta emphasizes connection and impact through technology, with AI becoming central to its identity by 2025–26.
identity: Meta has consistently valued altruism (connecting the world, building community), craft (shipping quality products, moving fast), and performance (solving big problems, making impact) across its careers messaging. Altruism peaked in 2016–2018 (zscore 1.7–1.3), then softened through 2023–2024 before rebounding in 2025. DEI language surged from near-zero in 2009–2015 to explicit demographic focus by 2020–2021 (explicit_demographic registers jumped from 0 to 11–12 chunks), then contracted sharply in 2026 (dropping to 0 explicit_demographic mentions, inclusion score fell from 0.57 in 2025 to 0.19 in 2026). AI mentions were absent until 2019, then grew explosively: 4.8% of chunks in 2022, 44% in 2025, and 100% in 2026—a complete pivot toward AI as the defining mission.
fit: You might be a good fit if you are energized by solving complex technical problems at scale, comfortable with fast-moving teams and calculated risk-taking ('move fast and break things'), and motivated by the idea that your work connects billions of people. If you value explicit diversity and inclusion messaging, note that such language has largely disappeared from 2026 copy, replaced by product-focused narratives around AI, wearables, and the metaverse.

sections.heading: The AI Inflection: From Absent to Omnipresent
sections.body:
AI was not mentioned in Meta's careers copy until 2019, when a single reference appeared in a job listing (4.8% prevalence). By 2022, AI mentions had grown to 8.3% of chunks, mostly in mission/brand sections. The real acceleration came in 2025: AI language jumped to 44.4% of all chunks (14 mentions of 'AI' and 1 of 'large language models'), appearing across mission statements ('AI is influencing the metaverse in mind-blowing ways'), process/logistics, and product descriptions. By 2026, the shift was complete—100% of mission_brand chunks (11 of 11) contained AI references, with 88 total mentions. The copy shifted from 'we use AI to help people' (2019–2022) to 'we are building the future of AI' with Llama, Meta AI, Muse Spark, and wearable AI glasses as centerpieces.

This was not a gradual evolution but a strategic reorientation. In 2025, the careers page began foregrounding 'Build the next generation of AI openly and responsibly' and 'Put your skills to work as we build for the future of AI — today.' By 2026, nearly every quoted section mentioned AI capabilities, hardware integration, or multimodal reasoning. The company's self-description moved from 'a social platform company' to 'an AI and hardware company building the metaverse.'

sections.heading: Altruism and DEI: Rise, Peak, and Contraction
sections.body:
From 2009–2015, Meta's careers copy leaned heavily on altruism—'making the world more open and connected,' 'building social value,' 'connecting billions.' This language peaked in 2016 (zscore 1.72, rawTopkMean 0.28), when the copy emphasized 'a better, more connected world for everyone' and 'people at the heart of every connection.' Altruism remained strong through 2018 (zscore 1.29) but began to soften by 2019 (zscore –0.43), and by 2023–2024 had retreated to near-baseline levels.

DEI language followed a different arc. From 2009–2015, diversity and inclusion were nearly absent from the copy (0 explicit_demographic registers). Starting in 2016, belonging-culture language appeared ('be yourself,' 'everyone belongs'). The real surge came in 2020–2021, when explicit demographic targeting exploded: 12 chunks in 2020 and 11 in 2021 explicitly mentioned underrepresented communities, women, LGBTQ+ employees, veterans, and faith groups. Inclusion scores peaked at 0.59 (2020) and 0.66 (2021). However, by 2026, this entire register vanished. The 2026 careers copy contained zero explicit_demographic mentions and zero belonging_culture language. Inclusion scores collapsed from 0.57 (2025) to 0.19 (2026). The shift was stark: from 'Diversity is a must-have for Facebook, not an option' (2019) and detailed ERG spotlights to product-focused copy with no mention of diversity, representation, or belonging.

sections.heading: Craft and Performance: Steady Emphasis on Speed and Impact
sections.body:
Throughout the period, Meta's copy consistently emphasized craft (building quality, shipping fast, learning quickly) and performance (solving big problems, making impact). Craft language remained relatively stable, with peaks in 2016 (zscore 1.29) and 2022–2023 (zscore 1.48–1.23). The core phrases—'move fast,' 'small and nimble teams,' 'build smarter solutions'—persisted across all years. Performance language similarly peaked in 2013 (zscore 1.50) and 2023 (zscore 1.18), with consistent emphasis on 'solving challenging problems,' 'making real impact,' and 'building something big.'

What changed was the *object* of that craft and performance. In 2009–2022, the focus was on social connection, community, and user experience. By 2025–2026, the same language of speed and impact was redirected toward AI development, hardware innovation, and metaverse infrastructure. The 2026 copy praised 'groundbreaking technologies' in 'computer vision, advanced optics and virtual reality,' and described Ray-Ban Meta glasses and Llama models as proof of 'pushing the limits.' The values—move fast, be bold, focus on impact—remained constant; the mission they served had shifted.
